title: Keep score, and beat the lazy machine
prompt:
Ms. Gridlock's urgent-ticket machine made 12 guesses. Fill in four small functions: `count` for the four boxes of the confusion matrix, `precision`, `recall`, and `baseline`, the score of a lazy machine that always gives the most common answer.

If the bottom of a fraction is zero, return `0.0` so the program never crashes. When it works, `python3 scores.py` prints the counts, the two scores and the lazy baseline.
expected_output:
tp 3 fp 2 fn 1 tn 6
precision 0.6 recall 0.75
lazy baseline accuracy 0.67
hints: `zip(actual, predicted)` hands you one pair at a time. Each pair lands in exactly one of the four boxes.
Precision divides by everything the machine called yes: `tp + fp`. Recall divides by everything that really was yes: `tp + fn`. Check for zero first.
For the baseline, count the 1s with `actual.count(1)`, the rest are 0s, and divide the bigger count by `len(actual)`.
explain_after: Google defines recall as TP/(TP+FN) and precision as TP/(TP+FP) [ml-054]. The lazy baseline is our own habit: if a real model cannot beat always giving the most common answer, it has learned nothing useful yet. Here the lazy machine gets 0.67 and the real one gets 0.75 accuracy, which is a smaller win than it first looks.
